When one element sets a style property twice, in its `style` attribute or with `style:` directives, the later one wins and the earlier one is dead code, often left over from an edit. Both places are reported.

The `style` attribute is read the way eslint-plugin-svelte reads it: a `{mustache}` inside a declaration is part of its value, and a `{mustache}` between declarations counts as every string or template literal it can be, through `? :`, `&&`, `||` and `??`. The declarations of those strings don't count against each other. A value with an at-rule, a block, or a `{mustache}` inside a comment isn't checked.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-dupe-style-properties": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<div style="color: red; color: {accent}">Saved</div>
<div style="color: red" style:color={accent}>Saved</div>
<div style="color: red; {isError ? 'color: crimson' : ''}">Saved</div>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<div style="color: {accent}; background: white">Saved</div>
<div style={isError ? "color: crimson" : "color: black"}>Saved</div>
```
